tara: Heads-up: found a weird parse failure in the starter app when using json_mode + fncall. Model stream included a trailing comma before newline and our JS helper choked on that chunk during streaming. Demo failed during onboarding.

tara: raw chunk:
```
{"task":"get_orders","limit":5},
```

jing: Oof, trailing commas in model output. Python tolerant parser silently strips trailing commas in the iterator; JS refuses to parse.

oscar: Also saw this combine poorly with auth retry. If a 401 triggers a retry the middleware reconstructs the fncall payload and we sometimes add an extra comma when concatenating fragments. Double-whammy.

mira: Quick mitigation: enable json_mode: "lenient" in client so the parser runs a small cleanup pass (strip trailing commas, trim null bytes) before parsing. But we shouldn't rely on sanitizing model output forever.

tara: Repro: minimal prompt in the starter-kit contains an example that leads to a trailing comma when model enumerates objects. Pasting prompt into issue now.

devex-bot: Created issue #2739 in redwood-inference/starter-kit and attached logs.

oscar: Proposed short plan:
1) add a normalization step in JS streaming parser that mirrors python's tolerant behavior,
2) add a fncall middleware test that simulates 401/retry + streaming to catch concatenation bugs,
3) update starter-kit sample to avoid relying on comma-sensitive formatting in prompts.

mira: I'll take parity on the parser. tara, can you add the minimal failing request id to the issue so i can write unit tests?

tara: Done. Added request id and a tiny curl repro.

oj: thanks folks — will pick this up in the SDK sprint. If anyone else sees weird model punctuation in streams drop it into #2739.
